# The `unattended` label

## What it means

The Human Lead tags an [item](./item.md) for [unattended](../core/attended-and-unattended.md) work from the companion. The companion records the tag in the desk's records, so a session cannot tag its own item. In an unattended run of the process work, the tag is what meets the first gate, entering Writing.

The `unattended` label is a GitHub label with that name on the item's issue. It shows on GitHub that the item has the tag. The record on the desk is what counts, and the label only shows it.

The label is a proposal of the product document of AI-Lore 1.0, and the Human Lead has not yet decided it.

## Where it is kept

The tag is in the desk's records, which the companion keeps. The label, if the proposal is accepted, is on the item's issue in the Space repository.

## What acts on it

The companion records the tag. The first build of the companion has no tagging and starts no unattended sessions, so no item has the tag or the label in it.

## Choices recorded here

- The product document does not say who puts the label on the issue. This entry does not say it either.
- The sentence that the record on the desk is what counts follows from the product document, which has the checks read the desk's records and says that a session cannot write them, while a session can write a label on GitHub.
